page_placements.theme: Tool-use and agent contexts: chat refusal direction weaker and only partly governs unsafe actions; separate action and injection subspaces

record.file_problem: Repository input only: the README and file list are provided, but the linked manuscript and result files are not supplied as text or read here.
record.tranche_reason: The README builds an agent-mode analysis and safety monitor on the refusal-direction finding. It reports direction measurements in agent contexts, but gives no outcome for the described causal intervention that would test whether adding or removing the direction changes refusal.
record.gate_note: The README reports d_chat projections, harmful/benign AUROCs, and alignment with an agent-specific direction; these are recorded below as findings about the direction in agent format, which none of the listed versions specifically covers. It describes an intervention procedure but reports no intervention result. Its in-sample agent-probe AUROCs of 1.00 are explicitly described as not evidence, so they are not rows.
record.test_reason: The README builds a chat-to-agent representation analysis and a safety monitor on the Arditi difference-in-means direction. It reports projections, AUROCs and cosines in agent format, but no ablation, induction or weight-edit outcome. Chat-to-agent format change is not among V6's transfer axes (languages, model variants, base-to-instruct). The repository lists a causal test (adding d_chat during generation), but no result for it appears in the supplied text.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The README claims the refusal direction 'rotates' rather than disappears in agent mode, and that harm is still encoded in a different direction (w_agent) that the refusal mechanism does not read. It says rotation is partial (~66°) in the 70B model and near-complete (~90°) in the 7B model. It proposes w_agent as an O(1) agent-mode safety monitor. It also notes that the final four-model manuscript supersedes some README figures.
record.recipe_differences: It computes a harmful-minus-benign chat activation direction, but applies it to a chat-versus-agent representation comparison and an agent-mode monitoring proposal. The README reports no all-layer ablation, refusal-inducing addition result, or capability-preservation result. Repo type: tool/research project; the README links a manuscript and results, but these were not supplied as text here.
record.method_sensitivity: The README reports different chat-to-agent direction alignment for Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct and Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3.

fits_no_version.finding: The chat-derived harmful-minus-benign direction separates harmful from benign agent-format activations in Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct (AUROC 0.96) but is near chance in Mistral-7B-Instruct (~0.5). Alignment with an agent probe direction is ~0.4 versus 'Low'.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The refusal direction's validity transfers from chat to tool-using agent format to a model-dependent degree.

fits_no_version.finding: Harmful prompts project 0.99 units less on d_chat in agent format than in chat format in Llama-3.1-70B (p=0.005, d=0.42).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Agentic formatting lowers the activation of the refusal direction on identical harmful prompts.

record.problems: Evidence here is limited to README summaries; linked manuscript and result files were not read. The README flags in-sample probe AUROC as invalid evidence and says estimates can depend on cross-validation partitions. It reports no outcome for the described causal intervention and no general-capability test.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted due to the 60-row limit. The README's in-sample agent-probe AUROCs of 1.00 were excluded because the README explicitly says they are not evidence.

untested.parts: No reported ablation removing refusal, no reported induction result, no capability-preservation check. A causal addition test is described, but its outcome is not in the README.
No test of affine, cone or multi-direction structure. The agent-probe rotation is a different construct.
The README asserts the model still encodes harmfulness in w_agent, but reports no separate harm-versus-refusal measurement.
No language, model-variant or base-to-instruct transfer; only chat-to-agent format.

missing.what: Causal test: refusal rates after adding alpha*d_chat at one layer to agentic harmful prompts the model complied with, with a random-direction control and over-steering on benign prompts. This bears on V1's induction part in a new setting. A behavioural baseline of refusal rate per condition is also missing.
Final four-model, 96-pair manuscript results, including the benign-control interaction and held-out AUROCs that supersede the README's exploratory numbers.

record.verdict_notes: Only the README was available. The linked manuscript and the causal_results files probably contain intervention results bearing on V1, so this study should be re-read from the manuscript before final classification. The stratified 'Expected Effect' table states expectations, not results, and correctly has no rows.

versions.untested_parts: No reported result from ablating the direction, adding it to induce refusal, or measuring preservation of other abilities.
No weight edit or abliteration result is reported.
No result tests whether attacks suppress the direction or whether training against ablation improves robustness.
The comparison of chat and agent directions does not test whether refusal is represented by an affine set, cone, or multiple directions in the same setting.
No separate measurement of harmfulness judgment and refusal decision is reported.
The README compares chat and agent formats, not transfer across languages, model variants, or base-to-instruct stages as specified in this version.
No comparison of refusal-training procedures or stages is reported.

relation.reason: It computes and applies the refusal direction to a chat-versus-agent comparison and a monitor, without testing whether the direction mediates refusal. Chat-to-agent format is not a V6 axis. The harm-in-w_agent claim rests on an in-sample probe AUROC that the README itself calls not evidence, so it is not a V5 test.

tranche.reason: Uses the Arditi diff-in-means direction as its starting point. The README reports only projections, AUROCs and cosines, with no ablation, induction or refusal-rate result. A causal-test stage (adding alpha*d_chat with a random-direction control) is described, but the README gives no results.

source_check.notes: The text is only the README and a file list. The final 96-pair four-model manuscript (docs/paper/article.pdf) and the later Llama-3.3-70B runs are not in it, and the Llama-3.1-70B figures appear to come from the v0_hackathon run. If the manuscript reports the causal-test (add alpha*d_chat, random-direction control) refusal rates, it could become a T3 test of V1 induction in agent format. No verdicts is correct.

statements.correction: Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct: AUROC d_chat on agent 0.96 and on chat 0.96; DeltaP 0.99 (chat minus agent harmful projection), p=0.005, Cohen's d 0.42 global. Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3: AUROC d_chat on agent ~0.5. These are likely exploratory-run figures; held-out status not stated.
statements.problem: None of substance. The numbers (0.96, ~0.5, 0.99, p=0.005, d=0.42) are on the right models and conditions. Caveat: the README says some descriptions come from earlier exploratory runs, and the 0.96 is not marked as held-out.
